name: Oliver Zhang
title: Shotloop: Make Videos with Code and AI, Free for Mac
description: Free, open-source macOS app that turns an idea into a short explainer video made of code, with Claude Code or any AI. Fix one shot; only it re-renders.
sub: Short videos with AI. Fix one shot, not the whole film.

features.title: Why one shot at a time
features.text: I made the explainers on this site with a pipeline that rendered the whole film for every check. Feedback was almost always about one shot: the subject too small, hidden behind a caption, nothing moving. Each check still cost a full render,

features.title: How it works

features.title: A voice-over and sound, on your Mac
features.text: A voice-over is off by default: the picture sets the timing, with captions on screen. Turn it on and the plan writes one line per shot, and the voice leads the cut: a shot lasts as long as its line, and the picture can land on the words. Or

features.title: How it compares
features.text: TOOL WHAT IT IS HOW YOU ITERATE COST Shotloop A Mac app for the whole loop: plan, 2D (HTML) or 3D (three.js) shots, AI checks, export with voice-over, subtitles, music and publish copy Per shot: only the shot you change renders again Free,

features.title: Choose your AI
features.text: Shotloop works with your own key for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Qwen and other providers, with Claude Code signed in on your Mac, or with a local model in Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible server. The A

features.title: Availability
features.text: Shotloop is out, free, and open source under the Apache 2.0 license (on GitHub). This version runs on Macs with Apple silicon and needs Google Chrome, which renders 2D and 3D alike.
